questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates CKAD proficiency in extending namespace-centric validation using core Kubernetes primitives: ConfigMaps, Secrets, CronJobs, InitContainers, PVCs, and NetworkPolicies. It also tests knowledge of jq for in-cluster JSON Schema validation and idempotent status updates.

## Key Concepts

- **Namespace-scoped configuration**: All resources operate within a single namespace boundary
- **CronJob with InitContainer tooling**: InitContainer prepares the environment (curl/jq) before the main validation container runs
- **JSON Schema validation using jq**: jq processes ConfigMap data against the fetched schema
- **PVC-backed logging**: Persistent storage preserves logs across job executions
- **NetworkPolicy egress control**: Restricts outbound traffic to only approved endpoints
- **Status persistence in ConfigMap**: Validation results are stored for auditing and downstream consumption

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: ns-config-schema-validator
  namespace: <target-namespace>
spec:
  schedule: "*/7 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: installer
            image: busybox
            command: ["sh", "-c", "wget -O /usr/local/bin/jq https://github.com/jqlang/jq/releases/download/jq-1.7/jq-linux64 && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/jq"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /usr/local/bin
          containers:
          - name: validator
            image: curlimages/curl:latest
            env:
            - name: API_KEY
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: validation-creds
                  key: api-key
            command: ["sh", "-c"]
            args:
            - |
              SCHEMA_URL=$(kubectl get configmap validation-config -o jsonpath='{.data.schema-url}')
              curl -s $SCHEMA_URL -o /logs/schema.json
              for cm in $(kubectl get configmaps -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do
                kubectl get configmap $cm -o json | jq -s ".[0] * {data: .[1] | getpath($cm | split(\"-\")[1:] | map(.))}" /logs/schema.json > /logs/validation-$cm.json || true
              done
              curl -X POST http://validation-portal:8080/api/v1/validate -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" --data-binary @/logs/summary.json
            volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /usr/local/bin
          volumes:
          - name: logs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: validation-logs
          - name: tools
            emptyDir: {}
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Trade-offs

| Aspect | Trade-off |
|--------|-----------|
| **InitContainer vs. Custom Image** | InitContainer adds startup latency but keeps the main image lightweight and avoids maintenance of a custom image. |
| **jq Validation vs. Dedicated Validator** | jq is lightweight and universally available, but lacks full JSON Schema draft support. A dedicated validator (e.g., kubeconform) offers better accuracy at the cost of added complexity. |
| **PVC for Logs** | Provides durability and debugging capability but introduces storage overhead and potential bottlenecks in high-frequency runs. |
| **NetworkPolicy Egress** | Restricts access to only required endpoints, enhancing security but requires careful planning of all dependencies. |
| **ConfigMap Status vs. Custom Resource** | ConfigMap is simpler and requires no CRD management, but lacks built-in versioning and conflict resolution. |

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD abilities: scheduling with CronJob, cross-resource coordination (ConfigMap/Secret), PVC usage, InitContainer setup, and NetworkPolicy scoping. It emphasizes per-namespace isolation and minimal instrumentation for reliability.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob per-namespace scheduling
- ConfigMap/Secret usage for config and credentials
- InitContainer provisioning of benchmarking tools
- Logs to PVC and metrics to ConfigMap
- Namespace NetworkPolicy for restricted egress

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1beta1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: bench-endpoint
  namespace: {NAMESPACE}
spec:
  schedule: "*/15 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
            - name: install-tools
              image: alpine:3.18
              command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache wrk && sleep 1"]
          containers:
            - name: bench
              image: appropriate/curl
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "wrk -t2 -c50 -d30s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $BENCH_TOKEN\" $BENCH_ENDPOINT || true"]
              envFrom:
                - configMapRef:
                    name: bench-config
              env:
                - name: BENCH_ENDPOINT
                  valueFrom:
                    configMapKeyRef:
                      name: bench-config
                      key: endpoint
                - name: BENCH_TOKEN
                  valueFrom:
                    secretKeyRef:
                      name: bench-secret
                      key: token
              volumeMounts:
                - name: logs
                  mountPath: /logs
          volumes:
            - name: logs
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: bench-logs
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle token rotation without restarting all CronJobs?
- How would you scale probes and tolerations to handle namespace density?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This checks secure defaults and practical CKAD patterns: ConfigMap/Secret usage, correct SecurityContext, and health checks.

## Key Concepts
- SecurityContext: runAsNonRoot, runAsUser, readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities: drop: ALL
- ConfigMap and Secret mounting into containers
- Resource requests/limits
- Liveness and readiness probes
- ClusterIP service exposure

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal Deployment skeleton (yaml)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: flask-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: flask-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: flask-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: flask
        image: python:3.11-slim
        command: ["python", "/app/main.py"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: app-config
          mountPath: /app/config
        - name: api-key
          mountPath: /secrets
          readOnly: true
        securityContext:
          runAsUser: 1001
          runAsNonRoot: true
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 5000
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 5000
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "200m"
            memory: "256Mi"
      volumes:
      - name: app-config
        configMap:
          name: flask-config
      - name: api-key
        secret:
          secretName: flask-api-key
```

```yaml
# Minimal Service skeleton
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: flask-service
spec:
  selector:
    app: flask-app
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 5000
  type: ClusterIP
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you rotate the API_KEY secret without downtime?
- What are the trade-offs of using readOnlyRootFilesystem in production?

    matchLabels:
      app: manifest-guard
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: manifest-guard

## Why This Question Is Asked

This question evaluates a candidate's ability to design production-ready, per-namespace observability data flows—a critical skill for platform engineers and SREs. It tests familiarity with Kubernetes security primitives, resource management, and operational patterns that generic deployments often overlook.

## Key Concepts Tested

- **Per-namespace isolation:** Scoping a Deployment to each namespace ensures data locality and prevents cross-namespace metric contamination.
- **PVC-backed data flow:** Tailing from a PVC provides durability and allows pods to restart without data loss.
- **Security hardening:** NetworkPolicies, Secrets, and resource limits demonstrate a defense-in-depth approach.
- **Operational concerns:** Probes, InitContainers, and sidecars reflect real-world operational complexity.

## Common Pitfalls

Candidates often miss NetworkPolicy egress rules, underconfigure resource limits, or overlook the trade-offs between Pushgateway reliability and simplicity. Strong candidates will proactively discuss alternatives like Prometheus scraping or distributed tracing backends.

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: ns-backup
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
            - name: installer
              image: busybox
              command:
                - /bin/sh
                - -c
                - apk add --no-cache tar pigz
          containers:
            - name: backup
              image: alpine:3.18
              command:
                - /bin/sh
                - -c
                - tar -czf /backup/namespace-$(date +%F-%H%M).tar.gz -C /data .
              volumeMounts:
                - name: data
                  mountPath: /data
                - name: backup
                  mountPath: /backup
              readinessProbe:
                exec:
                  command:
                    - cat
                    - /tmp/healthy
                initialDelaySeconds: 30
                periodSeconds: 60
              livenessProbe:
                httpGet:
                  path: /healthz
                  port: 8080
          volumes:
            - name: data
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: data-pvc
            - name: backup

        app: config-watcher
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: install-tools
        image: alpine:latest
        command: ['sh', '-c', 'apk add --no-cache inotify-tools yamllint']
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:alpine
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config-pvc
          mountPath: /config/dynamic
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 30
      - name: config-watcher
        image: alpine:latest
        command: ['sh', '-c', 'while inotifywait -e modify /config/dynamic/*.yaml; do yamllint /config/dynamic/*.yaml && nginx -s reload; done']
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config-pvc
          mountPath: /config/dynamic
        env:
        - name: STATUS_URL
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: status-secret
              key: url
      - name: tls-sidecar
        image: envoyproxy/envoy:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8443
      volumes:
      - name: config-pvc
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: config-pvc
      - name: nginx-defaults
        configMap:
          name: nginx-defaults
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: config-pvc
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: nginx-defaults
  namespace: target-namespace
data:
  nginx.conf: |
    # Default Nginx configuration
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: status-secret
  namespace: target-namespace
type: Opaque
data:
  url: aHR0cDovL3N0YXR1cy5sb2NhbC9hcGkvdjEvcmVsb2Fk
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: config-watcher-netpol
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: config-watcher
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: internal-services
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 80
```

## Trade-offs
- **Inotify vs polling**: Inotify is more efficient but requires file system support
- **Sidecar overhead**: TLS sidecar adds complexity and resource usage
- **Single namespace scope**: Limited to namespace-level isolation vs cluster-wide
- **PVC dependency**: Requires storage management and backup strategies
- **Container sharing**: Process communication within pod vs separate services

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
CKAD requires practical mastery of node-scoped components, DaemonSets, hostPath volumes, and real-world log shipping patterns.

## Key Concepts
- DaemonSet on each node with hostPath volumes
- Log tailing with tail -F and sidecar shipping
- ConfigMap-driven batching (BATCH_SIZE)
- NodeSelector to target workers
- Readiness/Liveness probes and lifecycle (preStop)
- Resource requests/limits and rollback strategy

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: log-collector
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: log-collector
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: log-collector
    spec:
      nodeSelector:
        kubernetes.io/os: linux
      containers:
      - name: collector
        image: busybox:stable
        command: ["sh","-c","tail -F /var/log/app.log | /usr/local/bin/shipper --endpoint http://log-portal:5000/api/v1/logs --batch-size $(BUS_BATCH)" ]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /var/log
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "256Mi"
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 15
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 30
          periodSeconds: 30
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              command: ["sh","-c","sleep 10"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /var/log
      volumes:
      - name: logs
        hostPath:
          path: /var/log
          type: Directory
``` 

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test under burst log loads and verify end-to-end delivery? 
- How would you rollback a DaemonSet rollout if a regression is found?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD skills: PVC handling, InitContainers, ConfigMaps/Secrets, simple templating, manifest validation, and network policies. It avoids previous questions by focusing on label injection and re-validation flow.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainer tool installation (kubeval, yamllint)
- ConfigMap/Secret usage for config and credentials
- PVC-mounted manifest discovery and simple file loop
- Lightweight templating to inject labels
- Validation with kubeval/yamllint and conditional POST
- TLS sidecar and readiness/liveness probes
- Namespace-scoped NetworkPolicy restricting egress

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: manifest-tagger
  namespace: <target-namespace>
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: manifest-tagger
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: installer
        image: alpine:3.18
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache kubeval yamllint curl jq && echo done"]
      containers:
      - name: tagger
        image: your-registry/manifest-tagger:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: manifests
          mountPath: /manifests
        - name: tagged
          mountPath: /tagged
        - name: config
          mountPath: /config
        env:
        - name: TAG_KEY
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: tagger-config
              key: tag-key
        - name: API_BASE
          value: http://tagger-portal:8080/api/v1/summary
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
      - name: tls-sidecar
        image: curlimages/curl:7.88.1
        # TLS rotation logic assumed
      volumes:
      - name: manifests
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: manifests-pvc
      - name: tagged
        emptyDir: {}
      - name: config
        configMap:
          name: tagger-config
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test the end-to-end flow locally? 
- How would you handle a manifest that fails validation after tagging? 
- How would you scale if the namespace has hundreds of manifests per minute?
